Row.Text: Canals

Adds a Canal building to each age. Build it on a land tile beside the water, where the game would let you put any building; when it is finished the tile becomes a coast tile with a quay on it, and ships sail through. Dig the next tile inland and the cut grows, up to the age's longest run. Unlocked by Engineering, Shipbuilding and Industrialization. An option in Options, Add-ons, switches to one-tile canals instead: one Canal in every age, unlocked by Irrigation in Antiquity, with no limit on ships. Single-player games only.

Canals
Canal rules

By age: each age has its own Canal, unlocked by a tech, and canals grow longer and carry more ships as the ages go on. One-tile canals: one Canal in every age, unlocked by Irrigation in Antiquity and needing no tech after that, drawn in the style of the age being played, always a single tile, and any number of ships can pass it each turn. Chosen in the main menu, it applies to new games; chosen during a game, to that game. Canals already dug keep their own rules.

Canals
Basics

A Canal is a building that cuts a ship channel through a land tile beside the water. When it is finished, the tile becomes water and ships can sail through it; the next tile inland can be the next Canal, so a cut grows from the shore, one tile at a time, until it meets the far shore or wherever its builder stops.

A canal can join two seas, a lake to the sea, a river to the sea, or two stretches of the same river. Each age has its own Canal, and a [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP] can build as many as it has sites for.
Canals by Age

[BLIST][LI][B]Ancient Canal[/B] (Antiquity): unlocked by Engineering. Costs 300 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production. +2 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food, +2 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold. A canal is one tile long.[LI][B]Medieval Canal[/B] (Exploration): unlocked by Shipbuilding. Costs 500 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production. +3 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food, +4 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold. A canal can be two tiles long.[LI][B]Modern Canal[/B] (Modern): unlocked by Industrialization. Costs 800 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production. +4 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food, +6 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold. A canal can be up to five tiles long, with bends and branches.[/LIST]
One-Tile Canals

Canal rules in Options, Add-ons, can be switched from By age to One-tile canals. The three Canals above are then replaced by a single [B]Canal[/B], the same in every age: unlocked by Irrigation in Antiquity, it needs no tech in later ages, and it is drawn in the style of the age being played. Costs 400 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production. +2 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food, +2 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold. A canal is always one tile and is never built next to another canal, and any number of ships can pass it each turn.
The choice made in the main menu applies to new games; made during a game, it applies to that game from then on. Canals already dug keep the rules they were dug under.
Building a Canal

Choose the Canal from a City's production list, or buy it with [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold in a City's or Town's purchase list. The placement screen offers only the tiles where a canal can be dug (see Canal Sites).

The Canal is built on the chosen tile like any other building: on a tile the Settlement works it goes beside the Improvement, a bare tile becomes a rural tile of the Settlement first, and on an urban tile it replaces buildings of an earlier age. Like other buildings, a Canal takes one citizen. A Canal bought with [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold opens at once.
When It Opens

The tile becomes a Coast tile and stays water from then on. Ships can path through it the same turn. The canal is drawn with a channel through the land, quays and buildings along its banks in the style of its age, and boats moored where it meets open water.

The Canal's citizen moves onto the finished canal and works it as a fishing tile, and the Canal building stays on the tile with its yields. If the City cannot place the citizen there, the citizen is left for you to assign.
Other Civilizations

Computer-controlled players build Canals with production or [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold, on their own land, where a canal is worth digging: where it saves a ship at least six tiles of sailing, or opens a lake or sea of at least ten tiles. Their units sail through their canals as yours do.
Multiplayer
Canals cannot be built in multiplayer games.
Canal Sites
Basics
A Canal can be built only on a tile the new water would join to water a ship can sail: a land tile beside the sea, a lake, a Navigable River, or a canal already dug.
Requirements

[BLIST][LI]Flat or hill land owned by the [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP], within the area where it can place buildings.[LI]Water a ship can sail on at least one side: sea, lake or Navigable River; or a canal already dug or under construction, as the next tile of that canal.[LI]Ice and natural wonders that stand in the sea, such as Thera, do not count as water.[LI]Not a Navigable River tile.[LI]A tile the Settlement works, a bare tile within the area where it can place buildings, or an urban tile whose buildings are all from an earlier age, which the Canal replaces. A building of the current age, or an ageless one, keeps its tile.[LI]No unit on the tile.[LI]No resource on the tile.[LI]Not already a canal, dug or under construction.[/LIST]
Settlement Centers
A City or Town center next to the tile counts as water a ship can reach, so a Settlement can dig a canal from its center out to the sea or a river.
Longer Canals
Basics

From the Exploration Age on, a canal can be longer than one tile. A tile next to an existing canal, or one under construction, is offered as the next tile of that canal when the current age allows it. Ships can pass once every tile of the canal is finished.
A canal's own water never makes a neighboring tile a site by itself. A tile beside a canal is offered only as part of that canal.
Length by Age

[BLIST][LI][B]Antiquity:[/B] one tile.[LI][B]Exploration:[/B] up to two tiles.[LI][B]Modern:[/B] up to five tiles. A canal can bend and branch, as long as every tile reaches open water through the canal; it is dug from the shore inward, one tile at a time.[/LIST]
Across Settlements

A canal can run from one [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement's[/TIP] land into another's. Each tile is built or bought by the Settlement that owns it, and the tiles together form one waterway.
Cliffs and Locks

A canal can be cut through a tile with cliffs along its edges, and once it opens, ships can cross every edge of the tile. Where the channel meets a cliff shore, the canal is drawn with a lock: a stone chamber with gates, a gatehouse and a water wheel. The lock does not affect movement.
Ships and Yields
Passage
Naval units and embarked units can move through an open canal between the waters it joins, from the turn it opens.
Traffic Limit
Older canals can carry only a few of your ships each turn:[BLIST][LI][B]Ancient Canal:[/B] 1 ship per turn.[LI][B]Medieval Canal:[/B] 2 ships per turn.[LI][B]Modern Canal:[/B] no limit.[/LIST]

A move whose path runs through a canal that has reached its limit for the turn is not carried out. A ship already sitting in the canal does not count against it, and the count resets every turn. The limit applies to your own move orders only.
Yields

A finished canal is a water tile of its City, worked as a fishing tile. The Canal building on it adds yields by the age it was dug in: +2 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food and +2 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold for an Ancient Canal, +3 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food and +4 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold for a Medieval Canal, +4 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food and +6 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold for a Modern Canal.
The cost is the [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production or [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold, the land tile, and any rural Improvement that stood on it.
